status: Exact-source and linked trace complete; successful PMIC read versus discarded error remains unresolved at runtime
findings: Command 12 calls battery_charging_control indirectly. get_charger_detect_status discards its return code and loads an uninitialized local output slot after the call. The binary confirms no preceding initialization or status test.

RT dispatch can return ENODEV/ENOTSUPP without writing the output. Source selects RT or BQ during initialization; mtk_charger_set_info can also assign the RT interface. The live pointer is not captured.
Both concrete charger-detection handlers pass flag 3371 to a PMIC getter, store its 16-bit result into the output and return success. The linked flag table maps to offset 0x0f78, mask 1, shift 5.

Both PMIC getters ignore the interface status and load a local output slot not initialized before the call. The compiler folds the normal implementation through bc11_get_register_value; this is not an extra BC1.1 hardware operation.

Both linked PMIC read interfaces call pwrap_wacs2 with read=0, write-data=0. They write the masked output only on success; errors leave that output untouched. Normal reads use a mutex except the existing suspend/reset with IRQ-disabled path; nolock still uses the existing PWRAP provider.
CONFIG_PMIC_HW_ACCESS_EN is defined locally in pmic.c; its absence from the kernel config does not disable reads. The emitted calls confirm reads are compiled.
pwrap_wacs2 returns -5 when its HAL pointer is absent; otherwise dispatches indirectly. This trace does not assert which error, if any, occurred on device.
The linked PMIC read interfaces have no printk call on their error paths. Zero matching log phrases cannot rule out a read failure.
interpretation: chrdet=39 proves the existing battery helper observed zero after callback return. It does not establish that a successful PMIC read produced that zero. A behavior change or forced cable-present policy is not supported.

next_discriminator.dispatch: Retain whether the existing command-12 callback returns success or failure; preserve the original call and output behavior.
next_discriminator.pmic: For the existing CHRDET getter only, retain normal/nolock entry and whether the original accessor succeeds with zero/nonzero or fails. Inspect output only after a successful accessor return; never inspect an uninitialized value for instrumentation.
next_discriminator.report: Use the existing one-shot post-return USB summary and ordinary software getters. No new hardware read, register write, role action, retry, periodic printk or retained-slot writer.
next_discriminator.limits: Cumulative outcomes are independent across callers and are not a per-call join. Missing paths, mixed outcomes or missing summary remain ambiguous.
next_discriminator.decisions: Successful zero isolates the native detection bit path; accessor error isolates transport/access error handling; dispatch failure isolates charger registration/control; mixed outcomes require preserved ambiguity.
